🌿 When to plant waterleaf in Nigeria

Also called Gbure (Yoruba).

Quick answer: Plant waterleaf in Nigeria from March to June and harvest from April to November. Grows readily from stem cuttings in moist soil through the rains.

PlantMarch to June
HarvestApril to November
Grows inSouth-South, South-East and South-West
TypeLeafy vegetables
Local namesGbure
JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec

■ plant   ■ harvest

About waterleaf

Waterleaf is a key ingredient of edikang ikong soup from Akwa Ibom and Cross River.

How to plant waterleaf well

Plant cuttings in moist, partly shaded beds.

Grows readily from stem cuttings in moist soil through the rains.

Diseases and pests of waterleaf

  • Leaf spotRemove spotted leaves.
  • Root-knot nematodesRotate beds.

Best states for waterleaf

Cross River · Akwa Ibom · Rivers · Delta · Lagos · Ogun

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant waterleaf in Nigeria?

Plant waterleaf in Nigeria from March to June and harvest from April to November. Grows readily from stem cuttings in moist soil through the rains.

What is waterleaf called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Waterleaf is called Gbure (Yoruba).

When is waterleaf harvested in Nigeria?

Waterleaf is usually harvested from April to November.

Which Nigerian states grow the most waterleaf?

Cross River, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Delta, Lagos and Ogun are among the best-known waterleaf states.

Can I grow waterleaf in my part of Nigeria?

Waterleaf grows best in the South-South, South-East and South-West regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack waterleaf and how do I prevent them?

Leaf spot: Remove spotted leaves. Root-knot nematodes: Rotate beds.
